topics.label: Lecture introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing and context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals, nomenclature, and central C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the basic concepts, naming conventions, and central role of C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how the three distinct recognition pathways initiate complement activation and reach a trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the downstream mechanisms by which activated complement eliminates pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the distinct clinical presentations and disease patterns associated with deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement and biomedical applications
topics.groupedBecause: It explores how pathogens evade complement destruction and how these bacterial evasion proteins are utilized in laboratory and clinical settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing remarks and indicates the topic for the subsequent lecture.
